title: What If Every Bat Vanished From Earth?

scenes.text: What if every bat vanished? The first change wouldn't be in the night sky. It'd be on farms.
In the United States alone, bats' pest control is worth at least three point seven billion dollars a year.
A real test already happened. A fungus called white-nose syndrome killed over a million bats in the eastern United States.
Counties hit by it later sprayed about thirty-one percent more insecticide, a study in Science found.
The same study linked that extra spraying to an estimated thirteen hundred more infant deaths over eleven years.
Take away the night shift, and the day shift pays. Nature's quietest workers turn out to be holding up the farm.

description:
What if every bat vanished?
Bats eat insects worth at least $3.7 billion a year in US pest control. When white-nose syndrome killed them off, farmers sprayed about 31% more insecticide.
